Using a peristaltic pump, rinse the tubing by passing dH2O through an inline heater set at 37 °C into a diamond bath imaging chamber mounted to a stage adaptor on a BX51WIF fluorescence microscope with a 10x objective.Next, in a 12-well plate, prepare combined Propidium Iodide (PI) and Annexin V (AnnV) dye using desired glucose solution (our lab uses a 3 mM glucose solution). PI, a cell exclusion dye, is used to detect generalized cell death. Apoptosis is measured using AnnV, which detect phospatidylserine when it is exposed to the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane during apoptosis.
Propidium iodide (MilliporeSigma, MA) dye solution is prepared by adding 7 ml of 3 mM stock PI solution to 700 ml of 3 mM glucose solution making a 30 mM final working concentration.Annexing V fluorescent dye (Invitrogen, CA) is prepared by adding 35 ml of stock AnnV conjugate to 700 ml of 3 mM glucose solution.Both PI and AnnV dye solution can be prepared in the same well as both dyes have different fluorescent wavelengths (700 ml glucose solution + 7 ml PI + 35 ml AnnV).Place the plate in a 37 °C humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2. Cover plate with aluminum foil to block out light, making certain sides are covered as well.In the warmed 12-well plate, add 20–25 islets to the PI/AnnV prepared well. Replace plate into 37 °C humidified atmosphere containing 5% CO2 for 15 min.While islets are incubating, change the peristaltic pump so that it is passing 3 mM glucose solution through the inline heater into the diamond bath imaging chamber rather than dH2O.After 15 min incubation, place the islets into the diamond bath imaging chamber mounted on the microscope.Stained islets are images using a Hamamatsu ORCA-Flash 4.0 digital camera mounted to s BX51WIF fluorescence microscope.Excitation is provided using a xenon burner supplied to the image field through a light pipe and filter wheel with a Lambda 10–3 Optical Controller.Regions of interest (ROI) are drawn around each islet and a brightfield (BF) image is taken. The white light source for the microscope is then turned off.Using cellSens Dimension 1.13 imaging software, fluorescent images are taken with 488 nm excitation/ 525 nm emission for Annexin V (GFP, green fluorescence) and 535 nm excitation /620 nm emission for Propidium iodide (TRITC, red fluorescence).
Note islets with dense centers seen on the brightfield image denote hypoxic cores. Islets with hypoxic cores should be excluded from cell death analyses as they may represent false positives unrelated to treatment (see Fig. S1).Repeat steps 4 through 10 for each treatment group. PI/AnnV fluorescent dye solution can be reused up to 4 incubation and measurements. Make fresh PI/AnnV solution for additional measurements.

steps.title: Prepare culture plates and incubator
steps.instruction: Label all plates, tubes and conicals; add 10 mL culture media to each cell‑culture plate and place plates in a 5 % CO₂ incubator set at 37 °C to warm.

steps.title: Make G‑solution for each mouse
steps.instruction: Prepare 100 mL G‑solution per mouse (90 mL HBSS + 10 mL BSA). Allocate 25 mL of G‑solution into one 50 mL conical per mouse, 1 mL into a 15 mL conical per mouse, and keep the remaining volume on ice.

steps.title: Place 15 mL conicals on ice
steps.instruction: Put each 15 mL conical containing 1 mL cold G‑solution on ice; the ice will inhibit collagenase activity before incubation and keep all pancreata at uniform temperature.

steps.title: Prepare collagenase (Solution C)
steps.instruction: Make 5 mL collagenase solution per mouse (plus an extra 5 mL, n + 1) by adding 7 mg collagenase P to 5 mL G‑solution; keep the solution on ice in 15 mL conicals.

steps.title: Euthanize or inject mouse
steps.instruction: Euthanize the animal with CO₂ or inject intraperitoneally 0.01 mL g⁻¹ body weight of Solution B; confirm lack of response to foot pinch before proceeding. (Optional) Exsanguinate by heart perfusion using a 1 mL syringe with a 25 Ga needle; do not disrupt the liver.

steps.title: Disinfect abdominal area
steps.instruction: Wet the abdominal fur with 70 % ethanol to reduce hair contamination in the IP cavity.

steps.title: Open abdomen
steps.instruction: Make a V‑shaped incision with standard scissors from the lower abdomen to the lateral diaphragm to expose the peritoneal cavity.

steps.title: Orient animal for cannulation
steps.instruction: Turn the mouse so the nose faces the surgeon and the tail points away; this positions the common bile duct at the rostral end near the liver.

steps.title: Secure liver with gauze
steps.instruction: Place a 2" × 2" gauze piece under the liver, stretch it across the xiphoid process and press down; fold a second gauze piece over the liver to hold it in place.

steps.title: Clamp common bile duct
steps.instruction: Clamp the common bile duct near its junction with the small intestine using a Johns Hopkins Bulldog clamp (Roboz # RS‑7441) or a tightly tied suture; avoid occluding the pancreatic duct.

steps.title: Load collagenase into syringe
steps.instruction: Fill a 5 mL syringe with Solution C (collagenase solution).

steps.title: Cannulate common bile duct
steps.instruction: Using a 27–30 gauge ½‑in needle or a 27–30 gauge butterfly needle attached to the syringe, insert the needle at the Y‑shaped junction of the cystic and hepatic ducts; advance in 1 mm increments, using a new needle for each attempt.

steps.title: Inject collagenase into pancreas
steps.instruction: Inject 3–5 mL of Solution C into the common bile duct to fully inflate the pancreas (volume adjusted for mouse size).

steps.title: Remove pancreas and place on ice
steps.instruction: Snip the common bile duct at its attachment to the duodenum, detach the pancreas from intestines, stomach and spleen, and place the pancreas into the labeled 15 mL conical that already contains 1 mL cold G‑solution (or into 1 mL collagenase solution if the direct‑injection method is used).

steps.title: Repeat for all mice
steps.instruction: Perform steps 5–14 for each mouse; limit to a maximum of six mice per isolation attempt.

steps.title: Incubate pancreata in water bath
steps.instruction: Place the 15 mL conicals directly into a 37 °C water bath and incubate for 7–10 min (8 min is typical).

steps.title: Mechanically digest pancreas
steps.instruction: Shake each 15 mL tube by hand for ~5 s until the tissue resembles pea‑soup consistency and no large pieces remain.

steps.title: Dilute collagenase
steps.instruction: Quickly add G‑solution to each tube to bring the volume to the 15 mL mark, thereby diluting the collagenase concentration.

steps.title: Centrifuge first spin
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes for 2 min at 1200 rpm (290 × g).

steps.title: Discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant into a waste container.

steps.title: Wash tissue pellet
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL room‑temperature G‑solution (HBSS + BSA) to the pellet, resuspend with a sterile 10 mL pipette, and centrifuge 2 min at 1200 rpm (290 × g); discard supernatant.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in G‑solution
steps.instruction: Add another 10 mL G‑solution, resuspend the pellet thoroughly.

steps.title: Filter through 420 µm sieve
steps.instruction: Pass each sample through a 40‑mesh (420 µm) sieve (Bellco Glass, Cat# 1985‑00040) into a separate 50 mL conical tube; keep each pancreas in its own tube to avoid overloading the gradient.

steps.title: Adjust volume for gradient
steps.instruction: Bring the filtered suspension to 20 mL with additional G‑solution.

steps.title: Centrifuge before gradient
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 1200 rpm (290 × g) for 2 min; decant supernatant and place the tube opening on a paper towel to remove residual liquid.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in Histopaque
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 15 mL Histopaque 1100 using a 10 mL pipette; the suspension should appear almost homogeneous.

steps.title: Density‑gradient centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge for 20 min at 1200 rpm (290 × g); islets will be located in the supernatant as floating white specks.

steps.title: Collect islet‑rich supernatant
steps.instruction: Decant the supernatant into a fresh 50 mL tube that already contains 25 mL G‑solution (from step 3); discard the pellet.

steps.title: Second spin to clean islets
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the collected supernatant at 1500 rpm for 4 min; discard the supernatant.

steps.title: Final wash of islets
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL G‑solution, resuspend the pellet, and centrifuge at 1200 rpm for 3 min; discard supernatant.

steps.title: Plate islets in RPMI
steps.instruction: Resuspend the final pellet in 10 mL warm RPMI (minimum 10 mL per plate) and plate the islets for culture.

steps.title: Prepare combined PI/AnnV dye
steps.instruction: In a 12‑well plate, add 700 mL of 3 mM glucose solution; add 7 mL of 3 mM stock Propidium Iodide (PI) to obtain a final 30 mM PI concentration, and add 35 mL of stock Annexin V (AnnV) conjugate. The dyes can be mixed in the same well.

steps.title: Incubate islets with dye
steps.instruction: Place the 12‑well plate in a 37 °C humidified incubator with 5 % CO₂, cover with aluminum foil, add 20–25 isolated islets to each dye‑containing well, and incubate for 15 min.

steps.title: Set peristaltic pump for imaging
steps.instruction: While the islets incubate, switch the peristaltic pump to deliver 3 mM glucose solution (instead of dH₂O) through an inline heater set at 37 °C into the diamond‑bath imaging chamber.

steps.title: Transfer islets to imaging chamber
steps.instruction: After the 15‑min dye incubation, place the islets into the diamond‑bath imaging chamber mounted on a BX51WIF fluorescence microscope (10× objective).

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Using a Hamamatsu ORCA‑Flash 4.0 camera and cellSens Dimension 1.13 software, first capture a bright‑field image, then acquire fluorescence with 488 nm excitation/525 nm emission for Annexin V (green) and 535 nm excitation/620 nm emission for PI (red).

steps.title: Exclude hypoxic islets
steps.instruction: During image analysis, discard any islet that shows a dense central region in the bright‑field image (hypoxic core) from cell‑death quantification.

steps.title: Repeat dye assay for each group
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 17–22 for every treatment group; the combined PI/AnnV solution can be reused for up to four incubations, after which fresh dye should be prepared.

steps.title: Rinse and dry tubing after experiments
steps.instruction: Pass dH₂O through the tubing and diamond‑bath chamber for 10–15 min, then run air through the tubing for an additional 10 min to dry before shutting down the peristaltic pump.
